newsitem.title: USA: US SPR oil sale may be out of interior bill.
newsitem.headline: US SPR oil sale may be out of interior bill.

text.p: A measure to sell $209 million worth of oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve may be removed from a House interior spending bill, but it still was not certain, spokespersons for House members who sought to strip the measure said Thursday.
"It's still in flux," a spokesman for Louisiana Republican Billy Tauzin said.
"The Rules Committee is working right now to take it out," a spokeswoman for Colorado Republican Dan Schaefer said.

Schaefer, Tauzin and Michigan Democrat John Dingell Wednesday asked the House Rules Committee to remove the SPR sale from the bill on the grounds that the House Commerce Committee, which oversees the SPR, had not approved the sale.
The committee passed a rule late Wednesday evening, but it was unclear how it treated the SPR sale.

Schaefer's spokeswoman said the congressman was hopeful that the sale would be removed from the bill. Schaefer argued that the SPR, established after the Middle East oil embargo in the 1970s, must be maintained as a buffer to oil supply disruptions and price shocks.
The House Appropriations Committee approved the sale as a way to fund the SPR's operating costs.

The House later Thursday was to consider the rule on the $13 billion interior spending bill, which spells out what amendments can be considered and what measures should be removed as inappropriate for a spending bill.

The House must approve that rule before it votes on the actual bill, but a dispute over whether to continue funding for the National Endowment for the Arts -- another issue in the interior bill -- could imperil the rules vote.
